title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes, on 13 June, Grothendieck again changes viewpoint and starts a 'fourth version' (quatrième mouture) of his notion of a 'contrée'. A contrée is a set F of 'figures' carrying two partial orders: ≤ (inclusion, sub-figure) and ≼ (subdivision). The aim is a purely combinatorial, order-theoretic axiomatics for the stratified, tame spaces of his tame-topology programme. This page isolates the axioms for ≤ alone.

C1 a) F is nonempty.
C1 b) Every family (F_i) of figures that is bounded above by some figure F has a supremum. So (F,≤) is a bounded-complete (consistently complete) poset, with no finiteness or directedness assumption.

Corollary: F has a least element, namely the sup of the empty family. Any element bounds the empty family, so a) is needed. NB: given C1 b), a) is equivalent to the existence of a least element. This least element is the empty figure ∅_F.

Definitions:
- A family of figures is 'compatible' (co-figurée) when it is bounded above as a whole; the inserted words read 'dans leur ensemble', i.e. jointly, not pairwise.
- Its sup is the figure it generates, its 'réunion', written F∪G, ⋁F_i, Sup F_i or ⋃F_i.
- A figure F is irreducible if F = Sup_{i∈I} F_i implies F = F_i for some i. In modern terms F is completely join-irreducible. The empty figure is automatically excluded, since it is the sup of the empty family.
- The irreducible figures are called multistrates, and their set is M.

The next page continues:
- The atoms of F are the multistrates below F, giving a map F → P(M), F ↦ F̄.
- Axiom C2: every figure is the sup of its atoms, i.e. the completely join-irreducibles are join-dense.
- Hence F embeds order-isomorphically into P(M), with sup going to union. The image L is characterised by: closure under unions of families bounded inside L, and, for each x in M, a smallest member A_x containing x.

This is the standard representation of a bounded-complete poset with join-dense completely join-irreducibles as a family of down-sets of the poset M of irreducibles. Geometrically, figures play the role of closed unions of strata (subcomplexes) and multistrates the role of closures of single strata.
errors: No mathematical error. The corollary and the NB are correct. The only subtlety is the empty family in the irreducibility definition, which correctly excludes ∅ from being irreducible; Grothendieck does not comment on it.
The struck-out first attempt at defining irreducibility ('F = Sup …') is abandoned mid-sentence and redone correctly below.

ideas.what: Axiom that every bounded-above family of figures has a sup; empty figure as the sup of the empty family
Contrée as a set of figures with two orders, inclusion ≤ and subdivision ≼, axiomatising stratified tame spaces combinatorially
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial/poset models of stratified spaces (face posets, Alexandrov spaces, exit-path posets); no exact modern counterpart with a separate subdivision order
ideas.usually_credited_to: tame topology programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); combinatorial stratified models by many later authors
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 announces tame topology and dévissage of stratified structures, but not this axiomatics

missed.claim: The fourth version of the 'contrée' axiomatics: a set of figures with two interacting orders, inclusion and subdivision. Inclusion is axiomatised here as bounded-complete with join-dense irreducibles (multistrates). This is an unpublished, abandoned attempt at a purely order-theoretic foundation for tame/stratified topology.
missed.quote: Contrée (quatrième mouture!) ... deux relations d'ordre ≤ et ≼
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Two-order (inclusion plus subdivision) poset models of stratified spaces could be compared with current combinatorial approaches (exit-path categories, refinements of stratifications, o-minimal cell decompositions). The axioms for ≼ and its compatibility with ≤ are the novel part, but they are not on this page.

missed.claim: The inclusion axioms coincide with domain-theoretic notions: bounded-complete posets, and representation by sets of completely join-irreducibles. Grothendieck does not mention this link, and it is not drawn in the tame-topology literature.
missed.quote: Toute famille majorée de figures a une borne sup.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor link; it suggests using Scott-domain and prime-algebraic representation results for poset models of stratifications.

deep.surprise_reason: The order theory on this page is routine. Interest lies only in its context, an unpublished fourth attempt at an axiomatics for tame stratified spaces, and the distinctive part (the subdivision order) is not developed here.
transcription_corrections: The top marker '[?]' is the page number 53.
'quand pas de [?] langage' should likely read 'par abus de langage et si confusion n'est à craindre'.
The insertion read as '{+deux à deux+}' appears to be 'dans leur ens.' (dans leur ensemble). Compatibility is joint majorisation, not pairwise, which matters mathematically.
The last lines should likely read: 'Les figures irréductibles s'appellent [aussi] des multistrates. L'ensemble des multistrates [noté] M'. The insertion is 'L'ens des multistrates noté M'.
'Si $F\in\mathcal{F}_{\leq}$': the subscript ≤ is probably a stray mark; the intended reading is F ∈ F.
